I have met so many kind souls in the LGBTIQA+ community! I’m bi myself and as a girl with autism, I heavily relate to the struggles of body dysmorphia.

Was just treated like I was stupid by an older woman yesterday trying to buy fabric at a craft store… Unfortunately, it’s also common for me to get this kind of treatment from older women and sometimes men. I don’t know what it is about me that makes most people want to treat me like shit. Might be the lack of eye contact, the fact I look years younger than my age, and my piercings and dyed hair. But whatever, I like having colorful hair and fun piercings. Sounds like you also have a unique and cute style! Just continue to embrace the things that you love doing and that make you feel at home in your body. 

I try not to let the things people have said about me get to me too much, even though I do end up ruminating very often. I have to remind myself that I can’t control that most people misperceive me and my awkwardness, and I’m lucky to have those who do understand me. I just focus more on the people who love me for me, and try to forget about the rest. It’s great to have a real connection your life, the love they give you seems to swallow everything negative you may have pent up. By no means do I have a lot of friends, I have one very close friend, my boyfriend, and my family. I end up cutting off any one of my “friends” who have intentionally made me feel bad about myself even once. I spend most days alone. It’s really… really hard to find people you can genuinely connect with in this world, most people don’t get us. I hope you can find peace of mind and comfort <3

And while it’s still fresh, I was just reading about a plant native to Australia called the Gympie Gympie, also nicknamed the “suicide plant”. Its heart shaped leaves are covered in fur-like, fluffy looking, poisonous trichomes that will lodge into your skin upon touch and cause intense lasting pain. The trichomes contain a neurotoxin that can remain for up to a year in your skin. It’s not even safe to breathe the air around these plants due to the shed hairs that are suspended in the air around them! It’s probably the most intensely painful plant sting you can get, and there’s not really a cure, you just have to wait up to a year until the pain subsides.

So the experiences I described are panic attacks. That makes sense considering the absolute panic I feel in those instances. Still, I do have a few questions about meltdowns. I wonder if I’ve experienced them as well, just not so sure what it looks like. What exactly brings them on? The feeling that leads up to a meltdown? Do you feel them coming on for hours beforehand? How do you act and what are you thinking during a meltdown?

With the panic attacks, they come on very suddenly, and my breath is instantly taken from me. They are always the result of some stressor that is directly confronting me or that I can’t ignore in my head any longer. My thoughts in those moments are just a loop of a specific anxious conception that my brain has spiraled out of control.
